cases.purpose: A synthetic utmp lists USER_PROCESS records for ttyA (twice, alice and bob), ttyB (mode 600), ttyD (mode 602), the case's own PTY, an empty line and an X ':0' line, plus DEAD_PROCESS and LOGIN_PROCESS records for ttyC. Four broadcasts (control/high bytes in arguments; a two-line stdin message; BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1; -n as non-root) reach ttyA and ttyD exactly once each, never ttyB or ttyC, and appear on the real terminal with CRLF endings.
cases.script:
t=$(tty); chmod 620 "$t" || echo chmod-failed >> rc
chmod 620 dev/ttyA; chmod 600 dev/ttyB; chmod 620 dev/ttyC; chmod 602 dev/ttyD
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py utmp 7:alice:ttyA 7:bob:ttyA 8:carol:ttyC 6:dave:ttyC 7:erin: 7:frank:ttyB 7:gina:ttyD 7:xsess::0 "7:me:$t"
export BASHWALL_UTMP=$PWD/utmp BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=$PWD/dev BASHWALL_USER=op BASHWALL_HOST=vmhost
wall $'esc\033[31m tab\there del\177 ctl\001 hi\351'; echo "rc1=$?" >> rc
printf 'l1\nl2\n' | wall; echo "rc2=$?" >> rc
BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 wall nb; echo "rc3=$?" >> rc
wall -n kept 2> err-n; echo "rc4=$?" >> rc
[[ $(< err-n) == *'--nobanner is available only for root'* ]] && echo nobanner-warned >> rc
/usr/bin/python3 norm.py dev/ttyA dev/ttyD

steps.expect: Broadcast message from op@vmhost \(pts/[0-9]+\) \([^)]*\):\x07\x07\r+\nesc\^\[\[31m tab\there del\^\? ctl\^A hi\\351\r+\n

cases.oracle:
wall.c header and write_doc/wall_doc: write TTY [MSG...] banner '
\a\a\aMessage from USER@HOST on SRCTTY at HH:MM ...
', message escaped like util-linux fputs_careful (control -> ^X, DEL -> ^?, bytes >= 0x80 -> \NNN, LF -> CRLF), trailing 'EOF
'; refuses when the target lacks S_IWGRP|S_IWOTH ('has messages disabled'); stdin is read to EOF when no MSG; wall walks $BASHWALL_UTMP USER_PROCESS records with a line (':' lines skipped), each line once, banner '
Broadcast message from USER@HOST (TTY) (DATE):\a\a
', BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 suppresses it, -n as non-root warns and keeps it, -g GROUP via $BASHWALL_GROUP_FILE members or $BASHWALL_PASSWD_FILE primary gid. util-linux term-utils write.c/wall.c are the cited behaviour sources; the candidate's TTY-path and environment interfaces have no util-linux equivalent, so these are contract cases. The banner date/pts are normalized by norm.py (regex stated in the file) before exact comparison.
cases.comparison: contract: exact normalized recipient-file bytes, empty skipped recipients, rc lines, and raw PTY regexes

files.mkutmp.py:
import struct, sys
# glibc x86_64 struct utmp (384 bytes): type, pid, line[32], id[4], user[32], host[256], exit, session, tv, addr_v6, unused
rec = struct.Struct('<h2xi32s4s32s256shhiii4i20x')
assert rec.size == 384
with open(sys.argv[1], 'wb') as f:
    for i, spec in enumerate(sys.argv[2:]):
        typ, user, line = spec.split(':', 2)
        f.write(rec.pack(int(typ), 1000 + i, line.encode(), b'', user.encode(), b'', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))
files.norm.py:
import re, sys
# Replace the per-run parts of a wall banner: ctime-style date and the sender's pts number.
date = re.compile(rb'\((Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun) (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 123][0-9] '
                  rb'[0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]:[0-6][0-9] [0-9]{4}\)')
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    data = open(name, 'rb').read()
    data = re.sub(rb'\(pts/[0-9]+\)', b'(TTY)', data)
    data = date.sub(b'(DATE)', data)
    open('norm-' + name.replace('/', '-'), 'wb').write(data)

cases.purpose: -g/--group against synthetic group and passwd databases: members listed in the group line (with blanks around names) and users whose primary gid is the group's receive the message; a group with no matching user and an unknown group deliver nothing; -g without an argument fails.
cases.script:
for f in ttyA ttyD ttyE ttyF; do chmod 620 dev/$f; done
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py utmp 7:alice:ttyA 7:bob:ttyA 7:frank:ttyE 7:gina:ttyD 7:hal:ttyF
export BASHWALL_UTMP=$PWD/utmp BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=$PWD/dev BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1
export BASHWALL_GROUP_FILE=$PWD/group BASHWALL_PASSWD_FILE=$PWD/passwd
wall -g staff s1; echo "staff=$?" > rc
wall --group=ops o1; echo "ops=$?" >> rc
wall -g empty e1; echo "empty=$?" >> rc
wall -g nosuch z1; echo "nosuch=$?" >> rc
wall -g 2> err; echo "missing=$?" >> rc
[[ $(< err) == *'option requires an argument: -g'* ]] && echo missing-diagnosed >> rc
